editorial.headline: Leather Accessory Making, Open Nationally and Usable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 14132 covers cut-and-sewn leather or imitation-leather accessories, open across every business scale and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 14132 is a manufacturing code for finished clothing accessories made from leather or imitation leather. Its scope is practical and workshop-based: the activity is the cutting and sewing of materials into ready-to-use accessories, including hats, gloves, belts, headbands, hairnets, furred-leather head coverings, and parts of those products. The emphasis is not on raw leather processing or general apparel; it is on the making of accessory items that are already shaped, stitched, and prepared for use.

That makes the code relevant for businesses whose core production sits in the accessory layer of fashion and personal goods. A founder registering under this activity should be able to recognise the work in the verbs of the scope: cutting, sewing, and finishing leather or imitation-leather items into usable products. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so it can describe anything from a small specialised maker to a larger manufacturing operation, provided the registered activity remains within the stated accessory scope.

The national PMA position is clear. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership figure of 100%. In plain English, the national classification does not itself impose a foreign-share cap below full ownership for this activity. The source named in the record is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, and the relevant number is straightforward: 100% is the foreign-ownership ceiling recorded here.

The Bali reading is also clean, and it matters because Bali applies a province-level moratorium rule to PMA registration for low and medium-low risk KBLI. For this code, however, the record does not mark a block. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason given is: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium”. That means the honest conclusion is not a hidden Bali prohibition, nor a separate Bali percentage. Based on this record, KBLI 14132 is nationally open and not blocked by the Bali moratorium for PMA registration today.
